articles.title: India's Rice Prices Surge Despite Record Stocks of 55 Million Tonnes
articles.excerpt: Southern premium varieties such as Sona Masoori have nearly doubled in a year after a weak monsoon, while the government's record reserves hold mostly common rice that southern consumers do not buy.
articles.image_caption: A worker pours rice grain at a warehouse in India.
articles.nri_angle: India supplies nearly 40% of global rice trade, so export curbs to cool domestic prices could tighten overseas supplies of premium varieties like Sona Masoori.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Amul to Wow! Momo, Indian Food Brands Are Going Global
articles.excerpt: Amul milk is in 38 US states, Parle exports to 150-plus countries and LT Foods just bought a US brand: India's food companies are manufacturing, partnering and acquiring their way into mainstream overseas supermarkets.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers in the US, Canada, the Gulf and Europe will increasingly find Amul, Parle, Haldiram's and Wow! Momo products in mainstream supermarkets, made locally to the tastes they grew up with.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FSSAI Confines Bisleri Action to One Goa Batch; Company Says Stock Is Gone
articles.excerpt: The regulator clarified that only Batch GO 270 was found non-compliant and barred from sale. Bisleri says no stock of the batch remains, all 143 plants are running, and it disputes the PAH findings.
articles.image_caption: Cases of Bisleri packaged drinking water bottles at a retail outlet.
articles.nri_angle: Bisleri is the packaged-water brand most Indian households and visiting NRIs default to; the clarification separates a one-batch order from the brand-wide ban rumours circulating online.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FSSAI Suspends Licences of Five Nutraceutical Makers Over Safety Violations
articles.excerpt: Vedant Remedies scored 12% on compliance and two makers were not operating from their licensed premises at all, the food regulator said, suspending all five licences with immediate effect.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers who buy Indian-made supplements can check the maker name on the label against the five suspended manufacturers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaipur's Vinita Somani Cooked Through Chemotherapy, Then Trained Nearly 200 Women
articles.excerpt: Diagnosed with breast cancer in 2011 after losing both parents and an aunt to the disease, she built a garage-kitchen hobby into Appetite, a bakery school branch, and a second career supporting other patients.
articles.nri_angle: A Jaipur home chef's garage-kitchen classes became a training pipeline through which nearly 200 women now earn from baking and cooking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

rows: Days of bakery workshop in July 2026
data_cards.title: Women Empowered Through Cooking

articles.title: Krish Ashok Takes Food Myths From the Kitchen to the Body in 'Masala Body'
articles.excerpt: The Masala Lab author's new book explains what the stomach, liver and intestines actually do, so readers can test the next frightening food forward themselves.
articles.image_caption: Author Krish Ashok with his new book, Masala Body: An Engineer's Guide to Eating. The book applies first-principles science to digestion and nutrition myths.
articles.nri_angle: Ashok's science-first approach helps diaspora cooks adapt Indian recipes to substituted ingredients and different kitchens abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Chefs and a Label-Reader Carry Food Into the First TIME100 Next India List
articles.excerpt: Prateek Sadhu, Hussain Shahzad, New York's Chintan Pandya and creator Revant 'FoodPharmer' Himatsingka are the food names on TIME's inaugural 100-strong India list.
articles.image_caption: The three covers of TIME's inaugural TIME100 Next India issue, featuring Alia Bhatt, Skyroot co-founder Pawan Kumar Chandana, and filmmakers Theja Rio, Aryan Khan and Payal Kapadia. The 100-name list includes chefs Prateek Sadhu, Hussain Shahzad and Chintan Pandya and creator Revant Himatsingka from the food world.
articles.nri_angle: Chintan Pandya's New York kitchens put the diaspora inside India's culinary story, and FoodPharmer's label videos are staples of Indian family group chats worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Inaugural gala at Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai

articles.title: Surrey Village Chef Kaiyum Dewan Khan Named UK's Best at BCA Awards
articles.excerpt: The Spice Lounge head chef took BCA Chef of the Year 2026 at a London gala, after a 55-finalist national cook-off — the Mytchett restaurant's third honour this year.
articles.nri_angle: The BCA awards celebrate the British-Bangladeshi curry industry, a backbone of South Asian dining in the UK; a village restaurant in Surrey taking the national chef title is a diaspora small-business story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai’s Eleftheria Konark Named Best Indian Cheese at World Cheese Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: The Bhandup-made chariot-wheel cheese led a four-award haul for India in Córdoba, seven months after Prime Minister Modi praised the same brand for its Brazil medals.

sources.label: Western Grocer (Guild of Fine Food release)

articles.nri_angle: An Indian artisanal cheese winning a country trophy in blind judging in Spain puts Indian food craftsmanship on the global map for diaspora readers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Masala Omelette, Anda Bhurji Make TasteAtlas 50 Best Egg Dishes
articles.excerpt: India's two breakfast staples placed 20th and 35th on TasteAtlas's world egg-dish rankings, behind Japan's ajitsuke tamago at No. 1.
articles.image_caption: A masala omelette with vegetables, served on a white plate with tomatoes and parsley. The dish placed 20th on TasteAtlas’s ranking of the world’s best egg dishes.
articles.image_credit: Hiromi Kudo / Canva Pro via Curly Tales
articles.nri_angle: Both ranked dishes are everyday Indian breakfasts that diaspora kitchens already make from pantry ingredients — the masala omelette needs no specialty shopping to cook along.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala Kitchen in Taunton Named Town's Best Place to Eat on Tripadvisor
articles.excerpt: Mattancherry, a South Indian restaurant named after a Kochi neighbourhood, ranks first among 202 Taunton restaurants in the Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice Awards 2026.
articles.nri_angle: A Kerala menu topping Tripadvisor's rankings in a Somerset town is the diaspora's regional food culture winning converts far from Britain's big Indian hubs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Accent Named India's Top Standalone Restaurant for Fourth Straight Year
articles.excerpt: At the Hospitality Horizon Top 50 Restaurant Awards 2026, the New Delhi flagship kept its No. 1 standalone ranking — and parent group EHV International placed seven restaurants in the top 20.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers visiting India, the list doubles as a booking guide: Indian Accent in Delhi and Mumbai, plus EHV's Comorin, Hosa, Chor Bizarre and Fireback, all placed in the national top 20.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sitaphal, Fig and Smoky Charcoal: Indian Sweets and Regional Fruits Are Rewriting Ice Cream Menus
articles.excerpt: Makers are reinterpreting mithai and regional fruit as scoops — Grameen Kulfi, Rose Gulkhand, jackfruit and tender coconut — without displacing the classics, says Iceberg Organic Ice Creams founder Suhas B Shetty.
articles.image_caption: Custard apple (sitaphal), one of the regional Indian fruits now appearing in ice cream menus.
articles.nri_angle: The flavours travelling into premium scoops — kulfi, gulkand, sitaphal — are the taste memories diaspora families look for in Indian grocery freezers abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Sold Cupcakes at 18 for Rs 20. Then She Built Dream a Dozen With Rs 5,000
articles.excerpt: Megna Jain hid cupcakes under her Christ University desk, launched Dream a Dozen in 2018, survived a six-week COVID closure, and built a women-led Bengaluru bakery.
articles.nri_angle: A Bengaluru founder who turned college cupcake sales into a women-led corporate gifting bakery — a bootstrapped food story diaspora readers follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Couple Quits IT Jobs, Builds Rs 56 Lakh Meal Startup Serving 55,000 Meals
articles.excerpt: Diya Krishnakumar and Adithya Natarajan launched Wellfed in September 2024 with Rs 15 lakh. Nine months of 2026 alone brought Rs 56 lakh in revenue.
articles.nri_angle: A home-style Indian meal subscription built for busy professionals mirrors the daily food problem many diaspora workers face — and the dabba model behind it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
